name: Stamp duty (Mumbai, incl. metro cess)
value: 6% of the property value in Mumbai, including the 1% metro cess
applies_to: Purchase of residential property within Mumbai municipal limits by a male buyer or joint buyers
source_name: NoBroker, 'Stamp duty and registration charges in Mumbai' (updated 2 Mar 2026)
note: The NoBroker page is inconsistent: its summary table, 'current stamp duty' section and FAQ give 6% for male buyers, but an older rate table shows 5% including the 1% metro cess. Registered deals support 6%: Rs 68.10 lakh stamp duty on an Rs 11.35 crore World One flat in July 2025 (https://www.freepressjournal.in/entertainment/neil-nitin-mukesh-his-father-buy-a-lavish-apartment-in-mumbais-lower-parel-worth-1135-crore-report) and Rs 2.22 crore on an Rs 37 crore World One flat in April 2025 (https://www.freepressjournal.in/entertainment/actress-amrita-puri-buys-luxurious-house-in-mumbais-lower-parel-for-37-crore) both work out to 6.0%. The official rates are published by the Maharashtra IGR (igrmaharashtra.gov.in), which could not be fetched in this pass.

name: Stamp duty concession for women buyers
value: 1% lower stamp duty for a woman buyer: 5% instead of 6% in Mumbai
applies_to: Residential purchase by a woman as sole buyer
source_name: NoBroker, 'Stamp duty and registration charges in Mumbai' (updated 2 Mar 2026)
note: Announced by the Maharashtra government on 8 March 2021. NoBroker says the rebate does not apply to joint buyers. Check the IGR's current conditions before relying on it.

name: Registration fee
value: 1% of the property value, capped at Rs 30,000 (so a flat Rs 30,000 for any property above Rs 30 lakh)
applies_to: Registration of a sale deed or agreement for sale in Mumbai
source_name: NoBroker, 'Stamp duty and registration charges in Mumbai' (updated 2 Mar 2026)
note: For a Rs 5 crore+ luxury flat the fee is the Rs 30,000 cap, so it is negligible next to stamp duty.

name: GST on under-construction homes
value: 5% of the agreement value without input tax credit (1% for affordable housing)
applies_to: Under-construction (non-affordable) flats bought from a developer before the completion or occupation certificate
note: These rates have applied since 1 April 2019. GST is charged on the developer's sale price and is paid on top of stamp duty. Every flat in this dataset is well above the affordable-housing limit, so the 5% rate applies.

name: GST on ready homes (with OC)
value: No GST once the completion certificate (CC) or occupation certificate (OC) has been issued
applies_to: Ready-to-move flats with a CC or OC, including resales
note: This is why buying an OC-received unit saves 5% against an otherwise identical under-construction unit.

name: TDS deducted by the buyer
value: 1% of the full sale consideration, when the property is worth more than Rs 50 lakh; 20% if the seller has no PAN
applies_to: Buyer purchasing from a resident seller (Section 194-IA of the Income-tax Act, 1961)
source_name: NoBroker, 'TDS on sale of property' (updated 9 Aug 2025)
note: TDS is calculated on the whole amount, not just the part above Rs 50 lakh. The buyer deposits it with Form 26QB within 30 days from the end of the month of deduction. It is credited against the seller's tax, so it is not an extra cost, but it must be withheld from the payment. Different rules (Section 195) apply when the seller is an NRI. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income-tax_Act,_2025), so section numbers have changed; the rate was not re-checked against the new Act.

name: BMC property tax
value: Rate x capital value, where capital value = market value x carpet area x weights for construction type, building age and use
applies_to: Residential property in Mumbai (Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation)
note: The capital-value system has applied since 2015. Weights: RCC building 1, building built after 1985 1, residential use 1. NoBroker says homes under 500 sq ft are exempt and homes of 500 to 700 sq ft get a 60% concession, with a 2% penalty after the 30 June due date. NoBroker's worked example of the rate is arithmetically wrong, so no rate is recorded here. Actual bills are on the BMC property-tax portal.

name: Tax on rental income
value: Rent less municipal taxes paid (net annual value), less a flat 30% standard deduction, is taxed at your slab rate; home-loan interest on a let-out flat is also deductible
applies_to: Rental income from a let-out residential property (income from house property)
source_name: Digit Insurance, 'Section 24 of the Income Tax Act'
note: rate_pct is the standard deduction, not a tax rate. The 30% deduction applies whatever the actual repair costs. Digit says there is no limit on interest deduction for a let-out property. The Income Tax Department's AY 2026-27 help page (https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/individual/return-applicable-1) lists the interest limit for a let-out property as 'actual value without any limit' under the new regime. Also confirmed by NoBroker (https://www.nobroker.in/blog/tax-on-rental-income/, updated 2 Nov 2026).

name: Leave-and-licence (rent) agreement registration
value: Stamp duty of 0.25% of the total consideration, plus a registration fee of Rs 1,000 in urban areas (Rs 500 in rural areas)
source_name: NoBroker, rental agreement page (Maharashtra row of state table)
note: Sources conflict. NoBroker's Mumbai stamp-duty FAQ (https://www.nobroker.in/blog/stamp-duty-and-registration-charges-in-mumbai/) gives the same 0.25% stamp duty but says it is capped at Rs 25,000, puts registration at 1% of the agreement value, and says registration is mandatory for agreements over 11 months. The Rs 1,000 fee from the state table is used here. In Maharashtra the agreements are registered online through the IGR's e-registration service. Not verified against an IGR page in this pass.

name: Holding period for long-term capital gains
value: More than 24 months; a shorter holding is a short-term gain taxed at your slab rate
source_name: Digit Insurance, 'Difference between long-term and short-term capital gains'
note: The period was previously 36 months, per Digit's capital gains page (https://www.godigit.com/income-tax/capital-gains-tax). Digit says short-term gains other than on listed equity (Section 111A) are taxed at regular income-tax rates.

name: Long-term capital gains tax on sale
value: 12.5% of the gain, without indexation, plus surcharge and cess, for transfers on or after 23 July 2024
applies_to: Sale of a flat held for more than 24 months
source_name: NoBroker, 'Section 54F of the Income Tax Act' (updated 9 Feb 2026)
note: NoBroker says sales of long-term assets after 23 July 2024 are taxed at 12.5% without indexation. Digit (https://www.godigit.com/income-tax/difference-between-long-term-and-short-term-capital-gains) confirms the 12.5% rate and that Budget 2024 removed indexation. Before Budget 2024 the rate was 20% with indexation. Not captured here: a later amendment to the Finance (No. 2) Bill 2024 is widely reported to let resident individuals and HUFs pick the old indexed method for land or buildings bought before 23 July 2024. No fetched source confirmed it in this pass, so verify before relying on it. The Income-tax Act, 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026 with new section numbers.

name: Section 54: reinvest in another home
value: LTCG from selling a home is exempt to the extent reinvested in one residential house in India, bought 1 year before or 2 years after the sale, or built within 3 years
applies_to: Individuals and HUFs selling a long-term residential property
source_name: NoBroker, 'Section 54 of the Income Tax Act' (updated 9 Feb 2026)
note: If the new house is sold within 3 years, the exempted gain becomes taxable. Gains not yet reinvested can be parked in the Capital Gains Account Scheme before the return-filing due date (https://www.nobroker.in/blog/capital-gain-account-scheme/). Digit mentions a once-in-a-lifetime option for gains up to Rs 2 crore (https://www.godigit.com/income-tax/capital-gain-tax). Not captured here: the cap on the total exemption introduced in Budget 2023, because no fetched source stated it.

name: Section 54EC: capital gains bonds
value: LTCG on land or buildings is exempt if invested in REC, NHAI, PFC or IRFC capital gains bonds within 6 months of the sale, up to Rs 50 lakh per financial year, with a 5-year lock-in
applies_to: Long-term capital gains from selling land or buildings
source_name: Digit Insurance, 'Section 54EC of the Income Tax Act'
note: The lock-in was 3 years before April 2018. Redeeming or transferring the bonds early makes the exempted amount taxable. The Rs 50 lakh limit is also given by NoBroker (https://www.nobroker.in/blog/capital-gain-on-sale-of-property/).
